question: Does sync-revealed Fixed Share mixing reduce stale embedding error versus strong fixed controls on real GCN training trajectories?
status: development screening, not novel algorithm or held-out scientific validation
corrections: Separate last observed embedding from self-fed predictor state
Score endpoint predictions before observing synchronization truth
Intermediate truth is evaluation-only, never gate feedback
Known Fixed Share is a baseline/application, not algorithmic novelty
data: LINQS Cora raw content and citation edges; deterministic custom split, not the Planetoid public split
schedules: learning rate multiplied by 0.1 at epoch 60

partition.method: random; not METIS; small graph algorithm screening only

predictor: SNI Algorithm 2-inspired self-feeding damped trend; lambda=beta=0.2; not reproduction of authors code
gate: two-expert Fixed Share, per directed partition pair; observation feedback only at sync, predictions frozen before observation
tuning: choose one gate rate and one constant mixture using development seeds across both schedules
screen_metric: mean per-boundary-pair relative L2 error during stale epochs, then average across epochs and seeds
gate_feedback: squared relative L2 error at synchronization endpoint only
go_rule: at least 5% reduction against the best of hold, predictor, and development-selected constant mixture on screening seeds in each schedule
additional_diagnostic: endpoint versus earlier stale-horizon winner agreement with ties reported; original 80% agreement assumption is diagnostic, not a separately tuned criterion
limitations: No downstream gate accuracy claim from trajectory replay
No communication or distributed hardware speedup claim
No proof of generalization beyond this small exposed graph
Closed-loop training and untouched graph validation remain necessary if screening passes
